title: Why Was the Reading Circle Empty?
locale: 山口県公立高校入試型
sentences: The children's center wanted to start a reading circle for younger students, but only a few children had registered.
Our class was asked to review the plan and find out why families were not joining the Saturday meetings.
The center had offered three different sessions, each with a separate age range, and parents had to choose one in advance.
Session A began at nine thirty and welcomed children aged six to eight, with only two of twelve places booked.
Session B started at ten thirty for children aged nine to eleven, and had nine registrations out of twelve.
Session C was offered at one in the afternoon for the same older age group, but only three children had registered.
Ken said the numbers showed that the youngest children were simply not interested in reading.
Mina asked whether we knew that, because few registrations could also mean that a session was hard to attend.
We spoke with ten families who had received the notice but had not registered, and asked what stopped them from joining.
Four parents said the early start was difficult because they took older children to sports activities on Saturday mornings.
Three parents wanted to stay with younger children during their first visit, but the notice did not explain whether that was allowed.
The other three families said they had missed the paper notice and did not know where to find registration information.
We reported that this small interview could help us find possible barriers but did not represent every family in town.
The center manager suggested moving Session A to eleven thirty, after many morning sports activities had finished.
She also agreed to welcome a parent for the first ten minutes and to explain that rule clearly on the new notice.
Our group made a large poster for the center entrance and helped publish the same details on its website.
After those changes, six more children registered for Session A, although the manager warned us that this increase did not prove which change helped most.
Some families might have seen the poster, others might have preferred the later time, and some might have wanted to stay briefly.
Ken admitted his first conclusion was too quick because a low booking number did not necessarily mean low interest.
Mina suggested keeping a simple record of how families learned about each session to improve future announcements.
The manager thanked us for listening to families instead of blaming them when the first numbers looked disappointing.
I learned that solving a problem starts with asking why people cannot participate, not assuming that they do not care.
fullTranslation:
児童センターは年下の子ども向けの読書会を始めようとしていましたが、申込者はまだ少数でした。
私たちは計画を見直し、家族が土曜日の会に参加しない理由を調べるよう頼まれました。
センターには対象年齢が異なる三つの回があり、保護者は事前に一つを選ぶ必要がありました。
Aは九時三十分開始、六〜八歳対象で、十二席のうち二席が予約されていました。
Bは十時三十分開始、九〜十一歳対象で、十二席のうち九席が予約済みでした。
Cは午後一時の回でBと同じ年齢を対象にしていましたが、申し込みは三人でした。
ケンは予約数を見て、幼い子どもは読書に興味がないのだと決めつけました。
ミナは申し込みが少ない理由は興味のなさだけでなく、参加の難しさかもしれないと指摘しました。
私たちは案内を受け取っても申し込まなかった十家族に理由を尋ねました。
四人は土曜の朝に上の子のスポーツ活動への送迎があり、早い時間は難しいと話しました。
三人は初回は幼い子に付き添いたかったのですが、案内に付き添いの可否が書かれていませんでした。
残り三家族は紙の案内を見逃し、申込方法も分からなかったと答えました。
私たちは少数の聞き取りから参加の障害を探れるが、全家庭の意見を代表するわけではないと報告しました。
責任者は朝のスポーツ活動が終わるころの十一時三十分へAを移す案を出しました。
責任者は初めの十分間は保護者が付き添えるようにし、その条件を案内に明記することにしました。
私たちはセンター入口の大きなポスターを作り、同じ情報をウェブサイトにも載せました。
変更後Aにはさらに六人が申し込みましたが、どの変更が最も効果的だったかまでは分かりませんでした。
ポスター、開始時刻、付き添いの許可など、申し込み増加には複数の理由が考えられました。
ケンは予約数が少ないから関心がないと考えたのは早計だったと認めました。
ミナは次の広報に役立てるため、家族が各回をどこで知ったか記録しようと提案しました。
責任者は最初の数字が少なかったとき、家族を責めずに話を聞いたことを評価しました。
私は、関心がないと決めつけるより、なぜ参加できないのかを尋ねることが問題解決の出発点だと学びました。

slashRows.jp: ミナは簡単な記録を残そうと提案しました / 各家族がどう知ったかについて / 次の案内を改善するために

slashRows.en: The manager thanked us / for listening to families instead of blaming them / when the first numbers looked disappointing.
slashRows.jp: 責任者は感謝しました / 家族を責めずに話を聞いたことに / 最初の数字が期待外れに見えたときに

materials.title: Initial Saturday reading circle registrations
materials.note: After changes to Session A, six more children registered; only ten families were interviewed.

questions.prompt: How many places were booked in Session A at first?
questions.evidence: Session A began at nine thirty and welcomed children aged six to eight, with only two of twelve places booked.
questions.evidenceJp: Aは九時三十分開始、六〜八歳対象で、十二席のうち二席が予約されていました。

questions.prompt: Which session had the most initial registrations?
questions.evidence: Session B started at ten thirty for children aged nine to eleven, and had nine registrations out of twelve.
questions.evidenceJp: Bは十時三十分開始、九〜十一歳対象で、十二席のうち九席が予約済みでした。

questions.prompt: Why did Mina question Ken's claim about interest in reading?
questions.answer: Low registrations could also mean families found the session difficult to attend.
questions.evidence: Mina asked whether we knew that, because few registrations could also mean that a session was hard to attend.
questions.evidenceJp: ミナは申し込みが少ない理由は興味のなさだけでなく、参加の難しさかもしれないと指摘しました。
questions.reason: 参加しにくさという別の理由があり得るため。

questions.prompt: Choose the true statement: A Session C was for ages six to eight; B Session C began at one; C Session B had two bookings; D Session A was in the afternoon.
questions.evidence: Session C was offered at one in the afternoon for the same older age group, but only three children had registered.
questions.evidenceJp: Cは午後一時の回でBと同じ年齢を対象にしていましたが、申し込みは三人でした。

questions.prompt: Why could the class not identify one cause of the later increase?
questions.answer: Several changes were made at the same time.
questions.evidence: After those changes, six more children registered for Session A, although the manager warned us that this increase did not prove which change helped most.
questions.evidenceJp: 変更後Aにはさらに六人が申し込みましたが、どの変更が最も効果的だったかまでは分かりませんでした。
questions.reason: 変更が複数あるので増加の原因を一つに絞れない。

questionSetB.prompt: Where would 'Those answers gave us several ideas for improving the event.' fit: after sentence 3, 8, 13, or 19?
questionSetB.evidence: We reported that this small interview could help us find possible barriers but did not represent every family in town.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 私たちは少数の聞き取りから参加の障害を探れるが、全家庭の意見を代表するわけではないと報告しました。
questionSetB.reason: 聞き取りの限界を述べた後、改善案につなげる。

questionSetB.prompt: Complete: Low registration does not always mean low _____.
questionSetB.evidence: Ken admitted his first conclusion was too quick because a low booking number did not necessarily mean low interest.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: ケンは予約数が少ないから関心がないと考えたのは早計だったと認めました。
questionSetB.reason: 最初の結論を修正する文を要約する。

questionSetB.prompt: Complete the word: Students made a p_____ for the center entrance.
questionSetB.evidence: Our group made a large poster for the center entrance and helped publish the same details on its website.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 私たちはセンター入口の大きなポスターを作り、同じ情報をウェブサイトにも載せました。

questionSetB.prompt: How many children in total were booked for Session A after six more registered?
questionSetB.evidence: After those changes, six more children registered for Session A, although the manager warned us that this increase did not prove which change helped most.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 変更後Aにはさらに六人が申し込みましたが、どの変更が最も効果的だったかまでは分かりませんでした。

questionSetB.prompt: What is the central lesson? A Families with low attendance do not care; B Ask about barriers before drawing conclusions; C Posters always solve every problem; D One interview proves all families are alike.
questionSetB.evidence: I learned that solving a problem starts with asking why people cannot participate, not assuming that they do not care.
questionSetB.evidenceJp: 私は、関心がないと決めつけるより、なぜ参加できないのかを尋ねることが問題解決の出発点だと学びました。
questionSetB.reason: 結末は原因を聞いてから考える重要性。
